boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten college-documented Oberlin traditions, from lantern-lit Tappan Square to organ concerts designed to be delightfully unchurchlike.

cards.title: Art Rental
cards.subtitle: Original artworks for a semester
cards.notes: Check the Allen Memorial Art Museum’s Art Rental details before the semester selection; eligible renters may choose up to two original works.
cards.short_summary: A 1940-founded program that sends original art into student rooms and local homes.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin says its Art Rental Program was founded in 1940 and lets students and community members rent up to two original works each semester for $5 each.
cards.source_title: Our Traditions | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: Availability, eligibility, and selection procedures are set by the Art Rental Program; the college lists a $5 per-work semester rental fee.

cards.title: Black History Month
cards.subtitle: A campus-wide annual commemoration
cards.notes: Look for the annually organized program through Africana studies and the Multicultural Resource Center, and follow the posted event details.
cards.short_summary: An Oberlin commemoration developed after the 1967 establishment of Black Studies.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin documents more than 30 years of Black History Month commemoration, organized in recent years by a committee led by Africana studies faculty and staff and the Multicultural Resource Center.
cards.source_title: Our Traditions | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: Program content and access vary by year; consult the college’s current events information.

cards.title: Big Parade
cards.subtitle: Town-and-gown art parade
cards.notes: Watch for the annual call to join a float or attend the parade, then continue to the performances in Tappan Square.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative procession of floats, bikes, costumes, music, and community-made spectacle.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin says the Big Parade began in 2002, became a cherished local ritual, and typically takes place on the first Saturday in May with a festival afterward in Tappan Square.
cards.source_title: Our Traditions | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: Timing and participation details can change annually; verify the current event announcement.

cards.title: Commencement
cards.subtitle: Pageantry centered on Tappan Square
cards.notes: If visiting during commencement, use the college’s current schedule and site guidance; ceremonies and reunion activities may use multiple campus locations.
cards.short_summary: Oberlin’s graduation celebration has evolved across Tappan Square, First Church, and Finney Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin identifies Commencement and Reunion Weekend as its largest annual campus event and documents its long history of ceremony, regalia, and Tappan Square gatherings.
cards.source_title: Our Traditions | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: Access, seating, and schedules are determined by the current Commencement and Reunion Weekend program.

cards.title: Community Engagement Institute
cards.subtitle: Service at the start of the college experience
cards.notes: Incoming students can review the Bonner Center’s current participation information and choose a partner-site service activity that fits their needs.
cards.short_summary: A coordinated service-day tradition connecting new students with organizations near Oberlin.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin says its coordinated Community Engagement Institute began in 1996 and gives incoming students service opportunities at partner agencies within 30 miles of Oberlin.
cards.source_title: Our Traditions | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: This is oriented to incoming students; the Bonner Center provides participation and accommodation information.

cards.title: Drag Ball
cards.subtitle: A student-organized celebration of drag
cards.notes: Follow the event’s current organizer guidance for attendance or participation, and respect performers, fellow attendees, and venue policies.
cards.short_summary: A college-sponsored, student-organized event with performance, runway competition, and dance floors.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin states that LGBTQ activists began Drag Ball in the late 1980s and that the college-sponsored, student-organized event celebrates non-normative gender presentation and drag.
cards.source_title: Our Traditions | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: Venue, date, admission, and participation rules depend on the current event announcement.

cards.title: Illumination
cards.subtitle: Japanese lanterns around Tappan Square
cards.notes: Plan around the commencement-weekend program and experience the lantern lighting from designated areas in and around Tappan Square.
cards.short_summary: A lantern-lit eve-of-commencement gathering rooted in a 1903 presidential inauguration.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin describes Illumination as an annual campus-community celebration and traces its lasting lantern tradition to May 1903, when Japanese lanterns marked President Henry Churchill King’s inauguration.
cards.source_title: The History of Illumination | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: The college described the 2025 event as free; confirm the current year’s date, programming, and access details before attending.

cards.title: Oberlin Rocks
cards.subtitle: Three painted glacial boulders in Tappan Square
cards.notes: See the three boulders in Tappan Square and treat current messages as temporary public expression; do not assume permission to alter them.
cards.short_summary: Class and founder memorial boulders that have become rotating painted message boards.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin says three glacial rocks in Tappan Square—linked to the classes of 1882 and 1898 and to the college founders—have been regularly painted for more than 40 years.
cards.source_title: Our Traditions | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: The rocks are in Tappan Square; observe any current college or city rules governing the space.

cards.title: Organ Pump
cards.subtitle: Friday-night organ concerts in Finney Chapel
cards.notes: Check the conservatory’s current listings for an Organ Pump, then arrive according to the venue’s published audience guidance.
cards.short_summary: Organ-major performances that deliberately pair musical seriousness with theatrical play.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin identifies Organ Pumps as Friday-night Finney Chapel concerts presented by organ majors in the Organ Pump Committee of Oberlin.
cards.source_title: Our Traditions | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current concert calendar, start time, and audience access with Oberlin before visiting.

cards.title: Decorating Mortarboards
cards.subtitle: A documented commencement custom
cards.notes: Graduating students can check current commencement instructions before decorating, since regalia and ceremony guidelines may vary by year.
cards.short_summary: A personalized cap practice within Oberlin’s evolving graduation traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin’s mission-and-values page identifies decorating mortarboards for Commencement among the college’s enduring traditions.
cards.source_title: Mission and Values | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: Relevant primarily to graduating students; follow current commencement regalia guidance.
